dm: Because I lacked devotion to the Dharma In the past and even now, I have come to such a state of destitution; Who would ever abandon devotion to the Dharma?
gm: Because previously and even now, I have been devoid of aspiration for the Dharma, Such destitution has come about; Who would forsake aspiration for the Dharma?

dm: The Sage has taught that aspiration is the root of all virtuous qualities; Its own root, in turn, is constant meditation upon the results of karmic ripening.
gm: Of all wholesome factors, The Sage has stated that the root is aspiration, And its root constantly is Meditating on the ripened results.

dm: Physical suffering, mental unhappiness, Various kinds of fear, And separation from what is desired— All these arise from the practice of misdeeds.
gm: Suffering and mental unhappiness, Various kinds of fears, And separation from what is desired Will arise from engaging in misdeeds.

dm: By performing the virtues intended by the mind, Wherever one may go, In that very place one will be honored By the rewards that are the fruits of that merit.
gm: By performing wholesome deeds intended in the mind, Wherever one may go, There, through that merit, One will be manifestly honored with the offerings of its results.

dm: Although those who commit sins desire happiness, Wherever they may go, Those very sins will, in that place, Utterly crush them with the weapons of suffering.
gm: Although those who commit misdeeds desire happiness, Wherever they may go, There, through those misdeeds, They are completely destroyed by the weapons of suffering.

dm: Abiding within the heart of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus, Their splendor nourished by the food of the Victorious One's melodious speech, Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through their virtue they become a Son of the Sugata dwelling in the presence of the Victorious One.
gm: Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cooling lotus, Whose splendor is produced by the food of the Victor's sweet speech, With a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through wholesome deeds one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.

dm: With their skin entirely flayed by the henchmen of Yama, they are utterly tormented, And molten copper, melted by a searing fire, is poured over their bodies; Pierced by flaming swords and spears until their flesh is torn into hundreds of pieces, They fall upon the intensely blazing iron ground as a result of their many non-virtues.
gm: Utterly tormented by the henchmen of Yama stripping away one's skin entirely, Molten copper melted by intensely hot fire poured onto one's body, Pierced by blazing swords and short spears, one's flesh scattered in a hundred pieces, Through many unwholesome deeds, one falls onto a ground of intensely blazing iron.

dm: Therefore, one should aspire to virtue, And cultivate it with genuine respect. Having undertaken the rite of the Vajradhvaja, One should cultivate the pride of self-confidence.
gm: Therefore, one should aspire to the wholesome, And meditate upon it with reverence; According to the method of the Vajradhvaja, Having begun, one should meditate on self-confidence.

dm: First, examine your resources, And then decide whether to begin or not. It is best not to begin at all, But once begun, one should not turn back.
gm: First, having examined one's capacity, One should either begin or not begin; Not beginning is best, But having begun, one should not turn back.

dm: By becoming habituated to this in other lives, Sin and suffering will increase. Furthermore, the time for the result will be inferior, And even that goal will not be achieved.
gm: Becoming accustomed to that in other lives, Misdeeds and suffering will increase; Other deeds and the time of results as well Will become inferior, and that will not be accomplished either.

dm: One should apply pride to these three: Actions, afflictions, and ability. Thinking, "I alone shall do it," This is the pride of action.
gm: Actions, afflictions, and capacity: One should generate self-confidence regarding these three. Thinking, "I shall do this alone," This is the self-confidence of action.

dm: Since this world, under the power of afflictions, Is unable to accomplish its own welfare, Migratory beings are not capable like me; Therefore, I shall do this.
gm: Since this world, powerless through afflictions, Is unable to accomplish its own benefit, Wandering beings are not capable like me; Therefore, I shall do this.

dm: If others perform inferior tasks, How can I remain idle? I do not act out of pride; For me, to be without pride is supreme.
gm: If others are performing inferior actions, How can I myself remain idle? I do not do this out of pride, For me, having no pride is supreme.

dm: When encountering a dying snake, Even a crow acts like a Garuda. If I am weak and feeble, Even a minor downfall will cause me harm.
gm: When encountering a dead snake, Even a crow acts like a garuda. If I myself am weak, Even a minor downfall will cause harm.

dm: For one who is despondent and has abandoned effort, How could there be liberation from misfortune? By generating the pride of exertion, Even the great will find it difficult to overcome you.
gm: For one who is despondent and casts aside effort, Is there liberation from destitution? But by generating self-confidence and effort, One is difficult to defeat even by the great.

dm: Therefore, with a steadfast mind, I shall overcome all downfalls; For if I am defeated by a downfall, My wish to conquer the three realms will become a mockery.
gm: Therefore, with a steadfast mind, I shall conquer the downfalls; If I am defeated by downfalls, My desire to conquer the three realms becomes a laughingstock.

dm: I shall triumph over everything; None shall triumph over me. As a son of the Lion-like Conqueror, I shall abide in this pride.
gm: I shall conquer all, And no one shall conquer me. I, a son of the Victorious Lion, Should abide in this self-confidence.

dm: Those beings who are overcome by pride are afflicted; They do not possess the pride of which I speak. The truly proud do not fall under the power of the enemy, Whereas those others are under the power of the enemy of pride.
gm: Any being who is overcome by pride Is afflicted, not self-confident; The self-confident do not fall under the power of the enemy, They fall under the power of the enemy of pride.

dm: Inflated by the pride of the afflictions, They are led by that pride to the lower realms; Their human joy is destroyed, and They become slaves eating the food of others,
gm: Those inflated by the affliction of pride Are led to the lower realms by pride, Destroying their human joys, And becoming slaves who eat others' food,

dm: The foolish, the ugly, and the weak, Are held in contempt everywhere; If even those ascetics who are puffed up with pride Are counted among the conceited, Then tell me, how much more pathetic are the lowly?
gm: Stupid, ugly, and weak, They will be despised everywhere. If ascetics puffed up with pride Are also included among the proud, Tell me, what kind of wretched beings are they?

dm: Whoever maintains pride in order to conquer the enemy of pride Is the truly proud one, the victorious hero; For they have certainly vanquished the burgeoning enemy of pride, And as they wish, they bring the fruit of the Conquerors to perfection for all beings.
gm: Whoever holds self-confidence to conquer the enemy of pride, He is the truly self-confident one and the victorious hero. Whoever definitively destroys the thriving enemy of pride, Perfects the fruit of victory according to the desires of beings.

dm: If I must dwell in the midst of the faction of afflictions, I shall endure in a thousand ways; Like a lion among foxes and the like, I shall not be overcome by the host of afflictions.
gm: When dwelling in the midst of a host of afflictions, One should endure in a thousand ways; Like a lion among foxes and the like, One should not be harmed by the host of afflictions.

dm: Even if great danger should arise, Just as a person protects their eyes, Likewise, even when peril occurs, I shall not fall under the power of the afflictions.
gm: Even if great peril arises, Just as a person protects his eyes, Likewise, even if peril arises, One should not fall under the power of afflictions.

dm: Just as one desires the joyful results of play, One should be attached to whatever task is at hand; One should find delight in that work, And never be satiated by it.
gm: Just as one desires the joyful fruit of a game, Whatever task is to be done, One should be attached to that action, And finding no satiety, rejoice in that action.

dm: Although actions are performed for the sake of happiness, It is uncertain whether happiness will actually result; But for one whose very work is happiness, How could they be happy without doing that work?
gm: Even if one acts for the sake of happiness, It is uncertain whether happiness will result; But for one whose very action brings happiness, How can there be happiness without doing that action?

dm: If one is never sated by sensual desires, Which are like honey on the edge of a razor, Then how could one ever be sated by merit, Which ripens into peace and happiness?
gm: Like honey smeared on a razor's edge, If one is not satiated by sensual desires, Having a ripening of happiness and peace, How could one ever be satiated with merit?

dm: Therefore, in order to bring the task to completion, One should engage in that work Just as an elephant, tormented by the midday sun, Plunges into a lake upon encountering it.
gm: Therefore, in order to complete the task, Just as an elephant tormented by the midday sun Plunges into a lake upon encountering it, One should also engage in that action.

dm: If one's strength declines, One should set it aside in order to resume it later; When a task is well-accomplished, one should leave it behind, Desiring the next and the next.
gm: If one's strength declines, One should set it aside in order to resume it later. If it is well completed, desiring the next And the next, one should abandon it.

dm: Just as a veteran warrior in the heat of battle Faces the clash of an enemy's sword, One should dodge the weapons of the afflictions And rise up to defeat the enemy afflictions.
gm: Together with veteran enemies, Like clashing swords on a battlefield, One should dodge the weapons of afflictions, And strike to destroy the enemies of afflictions.

dm: Just as one would swiftly pick up a sword Dropped in battle out of fear, So too, if the weapon of mindfulness is lost, One should quickly retrieve it by remembering the terrors of hell.
gm: If one drops one's sword in battle, One quickly picks it up out of fear; Likewise, if the weapon of mindfulness is lost, Remembering the fear of hell, one should quickly take it up.

dm: Just as poison spreads through the body By depending on the blood, So too will a fault pervade the mind If it finds an opportunity.
gm: Just as poison, by relying on the blood, Spreads throughout the body, Likewise, if an opportunity is found, Faults will spread through the mind.

dm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, Followed by a man with a drawn sword threatening to kill him, Is terrified of spilling it, so should the practitioner be focused.
gm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, With a sword-bearer standing nearby, Fearing the threat of death if it spills, An ascetic should likewise exert himself.

dm: Therefore, just as one would swiftly spring up If a snake crawled into one's lap, So too, when sleep and lethargy approach, One should quickly repel them.
gm: Therefore, if a snake comes into one's lap, Just as one would quickly jump up, Likewise, if sleep and lethargy come, One should quickly repel them.

dm: For every fault that occurs, I shall reproach myself and reflect for a long time, "By whatever means necessary, I must ensure that this does not happen to me again."
gm: For each and every fault that arises, Reproaching oneself, by all means, 'This will not happen to me again, I will act in this way'—so should one ponder for a long time.

dm: Thinking, "How can I become habituated to mindfulness In these various circumstances?" Through this cause, I shall desire to meet with teachers Or to perform the appropriate tasks.
gm: With the thought, 'How in these situations Will mindfulness become a habit?' For this reason, one should seek encounters Or appropriate actions.

dm: In order to have the capacity for all activities Before starting any work, I should recall the discourse on heedfulness And make myself rise with alacrity.
gm: So that before undertaking any task, One will have the capability for everything, Thus, recalling the teachings on heedfulness, One should make oneself rise lightly.

dm: Just as a tuft of cotton is moved to and fro By the coming and going of the wind, So should I be governed by enthusiasm; In that way, success will be achieved.
gm: Just as the going and Coming of the wind control the cotton fluff, Likewise, being controlled by joy, In that way, success will be achieved.

dm: From the *Bodhicaryāvatāra*, this concludes the seventh chapter, titled "The Explanation of Diligence."
gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the seventh chapter, entitled The Teaching on Joyous Effort.
